summary: You produced a competent, well-structured ethics report that meets all task requirements, uses the EA Code of Ethics and relevant case studies (NHS, VW), and reaches a justified 'not ship' recommendation. To reach the top band, develop secondary stakeholders more fully, balance your evidence on both sides of the argument, add visual elements, and polish language and referencing details.
next_steps: Add cited evidence supporting the pro-shipping side (e.g., industry data on release-to-market pressures or cost of delays) so both positions are equally substantiated.
Develop the chip contract company and health department as stakeholders: discuss how each should make their decision, not just Rachel and her company.
Include at least one figure or table (e.g., a stakeholder-consequence matrix) and proofread carefully to fix typos and garbled sentences.

To reach Excellent, deepen the significance of each issue and develop the chip contract company stakeholder, which you listed but never discussed.
criteria.C2: Very good (8/10). Your objective for/against arguments have reasonable depth and your recommendation follows from them. For Excellent, extend decision-making guidance to several different stakeholders — currently it is directed mainly at Rachel and her company.
criteria.C3: Very good (8/10). Your structure moves logically from arguments to case evidence to a well-supported conclusion. To reach Excellent, demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for ALL stakeholders — the chip company and health department perspectives remain underdeveloped.
criteria.C4: Very good (8/10). Four references including two external case studies with some quantitative evidence (fines, lost letters) show good research. For Excellent, add both qualitative and quantitative evidence on the pro-shipping side — currently your evidence is one-sided, limiting balance.
criteria.C5: Good (6/10). All required sections are present and references are mostly consistent IEEE style. To improve, use figures or tables (permitted but absent), fix language errors ('DICUSSION', 'ofprofessional', garbled sentences), complete reference [3]'s URL and access dates, and reconsider the tangential CNBC reference.
